entities.summary:
Blanche of France, a member of the French royal family, played a pivotal role in the medieval religious landscape of Western Europe.

As the fourth and youngest daughter of King Philip V of France and Countess Joan II of Burgundy, Blanche was groomed for a life of religious devotion.

In 1349, she entered the convent of Longchamp Abbey in Paris, where she would dedicate her life to a life of prayer and contemplation.
